transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I guess what brings me in is that I just keep planning my days around not having to drive over those high bridges. And, you know, if I absolutely can't get around it, I just white-knuckle it the whole way across. It's getting to be a hassle, so I figured I should come talk to somebody about it.
Do you feel this same level of anxiety or avoidance when you are in other situations, such as being in a crowded store, standing in a long line, or using public transportation?
No, it's really just the bridges. I don't have any problem with crowds or lines or taking the bus. It's just driving over those high bridges that gets to me.
When you are on those bridges, are you more worried about the height itself, or are you more worried that you might lose control of the car or be unable to escape if something goes wrong?

Well, I guess it's not really about being trapped or unable to escape. I mean, I know those bridges over the bay are built fine, and folks drive them every day without a problem. But... when I get near one, my mind just acts like the car could go right over the side. So I suppose it's that feeling, just the idea of falling over the edge, that really gets to me.
Do you experience this same level of fear or anxiety if you are in a high place, such as an observation deck or a balcony, even if you are not in a car?
No, not really. I can stand out on a balcony or look out the window of a tall building just fine. It doesn't bother me at all. It really just seems to be when I'm behind the wheel on those bridges.
